_description: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor equations: torque, power, efficiency, speed, and thermal models.

equations.name: Motor Shaft Power
equations.description: Mechanical power output at the motor shaft. Product of torque and angular velocity.

reference.text: Chapman, S.J. — Electric Machinery Fundamentals, §7.2. McGraw-Hill.

equations.name: Motor Torque from Current (PMSM)
equations.description: Electromagnetic torque produced by PMSM. Proportional to q-axis current I_q (torque-producing component). d-axis current I_d = 0 for maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control.

lambda_f.name: Permanent magnet flux linkage
lambda_f.notes: Material and geometry dependent. From motor datasheet.

simplified_form.description: For control purposes, use motor torque constant Kt

test_case.notes: At cruise: P=55kW, n=2000rpm → τ=262Nm → I=262/2.18=120A

equations.name: Motor Efficiency
equations.description: Motor efficiency accounting for copper (I²R), iron (eddy current + hysteresis), and mechanical (bearing, windage) losses.

P_copper.name: Copper (I²R) losses
P_copper.notes: = I² × R_stator. Dominant at high load.

P_iron.name: Iron losses
P_iron.notes: Eddy current + hysteresis. Dominant at high speed, low load.

P_mech.name: Mechanical losses
P_mech.notes: Bearing friction, windage. Typically < 1% of rated power.

simplified_efficiency_map.description: In practice, use measured efficiency map: eta_motor(P, n) from datasheet

reference.text: Miller, T.J.E. — Brushless Permanent Magnet and Reluctance Motor Drives. OUP, 1989.

equations.name: Motor Electrical Power Input
equations.description: Electrical power consumed by motor from inverter. Used to calculate current draw from DC bus and battery.
equations.chain: P_req (propulsion) → P_shaft_motor = P_req/eta_prop → P_elec_motor = P_shaft/eta_motor → P_inverter_in = P_elec/eta_inverter → P_battery = P_inv_in

equations.name: Back-EMF (PMSM)
equations.description: Back electromotive force generated by rotating permanent magnets. Determines minimum DC bus voltage required. V_bus > E_emf + I*R_stator.

Ke.name: Back-EMF constant
Ke.notes: = Kt in SI units. Equal numerically.

test_case.notes: V_DC_bus=400V. E_emf=399.5V → margin = 0.5V (inverter compensates via PWM duty cycle)

equations.name: Motor Heat Generation
equations.description: Heat rejected by motor. Sum of copper, iron, and mechanical losses. Drives cooling system sizing.

test_case.notes: At cruise: Q = 55 × (1-0.95)/0.95 = 2.89 kW heat → cooling flow required
